title: The Missing Band
subtitle: Regression to the mean in LISA, and the sampler that ends it — the numbers behind the demo (run OV50)
abstract_ja: LISA（ICASSP 2022）は 12 kHz の音声を 48 kHz に超解像する小さなネットワークですが、決定論的な損失で学習すると条件付き平均に収束し、6 kHz より上の帯域はこもります。解決策はアーキテクチャではなく目的関数です。入力に 8 本のガウス雑音チャネルを連結し、同じネットワークをエネルギースコアで学習すると、順伝播 1 回が p(y|x) からの 1 サンプルになります（τ = 0 は LISA そのもの）。ホールドアウト発話 12 件（話者 1 名、各 16 サンプル）で高域欠損は −12.61 dB から −6.85 dB へ、CRPS は 0.960 から 0.570 へ改善しましたが、PIT 端ビンは理想 0.118 に対して 0.182 で、まだ較正された条件付き分布とは言えません。

sections.heading: The problem
paragraphs: LISA (ICASSP 2022) is a small audio super-resolution network: 12 kHz in, 48 kHz out, 86,881 parameters as reimplemented here. It is trained with a deterministic loss on a one-to-many problem, so its minimiser is the conditional mean — and the mean of a random-phase high band has no energy. The output is muffled. That is not a bug in the model; it is what the objective asks for. LISA's own configuration (`det_paper`) leaves the band above 6 kHz **27.6 dB** too quiet on the held-out set.

sections.heading: The fix is an objective, not an architecture
paragraphs: Concatenate eight Gaussian channels to the waveform at the encoder input (+896 weights, 87,777 parameters) and train the same network under the **energy score**, two draws per step, on a distance that combines waveform L1 with a spectral term. The score is strictly proper, so the minimiser is p(y|x) rather than its mean. One forward pass is one sample; sixteen give the spread; with the noise at zero the network is LISA exactly. No discriminator, no diffusion, no second network. The recipe follows DISCO Nets (2016) and Gritsenko et al. (2020); new here are the target, the stochastic local implicit decoder and the diagnostics.

sections.heading: What the numbers say
paragraphs: Every figure is from the run's own evaluation, the JSON the demo reads: twelve held-out utterances of one speaker (p236), never trained on, 16 draws each. `det` is the deterministic reference with the same spectral term; `es_dec_erb_l0.1` is the arm the demo opens on.

sections.heading: What the demo lets you do
paragraphs: Pick a speaker, a rate (×4 or ×8: the same weights queried at twice the density) and a model; the network runs in the browser. **1 / 2 / 3** switch input, output and truth on one clock, so only the band above 6 kHz changes. Change the **readout**: one draw is what would ship; the mean of 16 is SNR-optimal and muffled — regression to the mean, made audible. **V** records your voice, band-limits it to 6 kHz and runs it through the network: training was English only, so Japanese is out of distribution — that is the experiment. **B** is a blind A/B test against the deterministic model; the tally is votes in a room, not an evaluation.

table.caption: Run OV50, EVAL12: 12 held-out utterances of p236, 16 draws, 104,950 steps. LSD in the repo's convention (decades of power, not dB) at the passthrough readout each arm wins ViSQOL on. Cost: one pass over 1 s of audio on an Apple M4 CPU, 8 threads, fp32.
rows: Parameters · cost per second of audio

caveats: **Not calibrated.** PIT end bins are 1.55× ideal, almost all of it in the top bin: the truth sits above all sixteen draws more often than chance — a level bias, not a narrow ensemble. These are conditional predictors with usable spread, not calibrated conditional distributions.
**Not a large evaluation.** Twelve utterances of one speaker; no FAD; no listening test. Part of the CRPS gain is definitional: a point forecast's CRPS is its MAE.

**Not comparable on LSD or SNR.** LSD is computed differently in every paper and cannot be set against LISA's published 0.81. SNR is inert here: an empty high band scores 18.99 dB, above seven of the eight arms (the true band: 41.60 dB) — never rank on it.
references: Kim, Lee, Hong, Ok. Learning Continuous Representation of Audio for Arbitrary Scale Super Resolution (LISA). ICASSP 2022, arXiv:2111.00195.  ·  DISCO Nets (2016).  ·  Gritsenko et al. (2020), the spectral energy distance.
